answer: Each bonded identity escrows collateral, so splitting stake across aliases does not erase exposure: correlated equivocation creates pairwise fault evidence, and aggregate slashing grows as k(k−1)/2 = O(k²) for k coordinated identities. Detection also triggers asymmetric depreciation of remaining bonded capital, applying a swarm-size-dependent exponential loss multiplier. Thus, a sybil operator risks more than the sum of isolated penalties; yarrow, lotus, and mirror are merely labels, not protection from linkage or forfeiture.
